newsitem.title: UK: Gehe says Unichem/Lloyds merger risky. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Gehe says Unichem/Lloyds merger risky. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: German pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe AG said on Friday that the possible acquisition of Lloyds Chemists Plc by Gehe's bid rival Unichem Plc would hold "substantial risks" for shareholders of both companies.
Gehe attacked Unichem's rival offer for the pharmacy chain in a letter to Lloyds and Unichem shareholders.
The second closing of Unichem's offer for Lloyds, which is currently worth around 633 million stg, was at 1500 GMT on Friday.
The second closing of Gehe's own bid, which is worth 650.6 million stg, is on January 10.
(Corrects value of Unichem bid and clarifies timetable).
Gehe's own bid, which is worth 650.6 million stg, is open until January 10. Lloyds shareholders have so far shown little enthusiasm for either bid.

Dieter Kammerer, chairman of Gehe's management board, said in the letter that Unichem's shareholders would gain more benefit from a buy-back of Unichem shares at current levels than from acquiring Lloyds.

"Both Lloyds Chemists and Unichem shareholders would face major risks and uncertainties as shareholders in a heavily-indebted merged Lloyds Chemists/Unichem group, at a time of volatile stock market conditions and increased speculation of rising interest rates," Kammerer said.
Gehe made a cash bid for Lloyds, while Unichem has offered a mix of cash and shares.
Both companies have until January 17 to increase their offers.
